historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Sunaina was a courtesan in ancient India, famous for her beauty and charm. She is believed to have lived during the Gupta period (AD 320-550). One popular legend about Sunaina is that she was visited by the god Krishna, who was so entranced by her beauty that he spent several nights with her. Another legend states that Sunaina was the lover of the king Prithviraj Chauhan, who was known for his valor and wisdom.

In another interpretation, Sunaina is a female form of the Hindu deity Surya, the sun god. The name Sunaina is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Surya-na', which means 'pleasing or dear to Surya'.
